premise.claim: Issue sgl-project/rbg#284: "By turning on pprof, we could observe details and the reason is that irrelevant Pods consume most of the memory" — the rbg operator's informer cache retains every Pod in the cluster because cacheOptions() only filters Service/StatefulSet/Deployment by the group-name label.
premise.reportedComponent: operator informer cache (cmd/rbgs cacheOptions / controller-runtime cache)
premise.patchedComponent: design of the same cache (KEP-284 revision 2 proposes a single-informer cache.ByObject Transform stub behind --pod-cache-scope) plus a prototype harness in test/podcacheunion; production flag wiring remains TBD
premise.evidence: TestCacheOptionsConstrainsPodCache fails on the base code: cacheOptions() has 3 ByObject entries (Service, StatefulSet, Deployment) and none for *corev1.Pod, so the Pod informer is unfiltered — see results/unit-head.txt (round 1) and results/round2/unit-head.txt (round 2 re-run on f8d67fa7: production code unchanged, still no Pod entry)

integration.note: Runs the PR's own test/podcacheunion correctness suite (//go:build podcacheunion) against an isolated envtest kube-apiserver 1.31.0, in both WatchListClient configurations, with -race off but the cache mutation detector on; resolves envtest assets from KUBEBUILDER_ASSETS or bin/. Round 2: also carries the median canary.

findings.note: Round 1 major A-F1. Round 2 status: the KEP now specifies the mechanism (marker never written into any workload template + key-scoped FilterSystemLabels exemption as a guard, keps/284-pod-cache-filter/README.md 'Marker and Backfill'), and names these two tests as the regression suite for the implementation PR. The tests stay RED on this head because the PR still changes no production code — that is the documented deferral, not an open design defect. They must go green in the implementation PR.

The guard the KEP itself names ('a test that group-name drift is still detected'). GREEN now and must STAY green when the implementation PR lands the key-scoped exemption; a flip to red means the exemption was implemented as a whole-prefix strip, which the KEP forbids.

Round 3: FIXED by d1c331ae — transform-campaign.sh now does `export USE_EXISTING_CLUSTER=false` AND TestMain pins `UseExistingCluster: ptr.To(false)`, so the campaign cannot escape to the kubeconfig cluster regardless of the caller's environment. Contract test green (results/round3-after-inversion/unit.out).

Round 2: no Makefile target or CI workflow references the podcacheunion build tag, so the KEP's evidence package is never compiled by CI. Fix: a CI step such as `go vet -mod=vendor -tags=podcacheunion ./test/podcacheunion` (compile check suffices; the envtest suite needs assets). Verified red/green bite in results/round2/harness-bites.txt.

Round 3: FIXED by d1c331ae — README item 4 now reads 'Node-name reads in RecordNodeBindings, Warmup and RBG reconciliation consume Pods from these scoped Lists; none uses a spec.nodeName field selector', naming the audited sites and why they are safe. Contract test green (results/round3-after-inversion/unit.out).

Round 3: FIXED by d1c331ae — medianRange now averages the two middle values for even-sized groups. The round-2 bug-canary flipped red exactly as designed (results/round3/integration.out: TestMedianRangeUpperMiddleForEvenGroups fail=2 in both gate configs) and has been inverted into a contract test; both it and the head's own TestMedianRange pass in both gate configs (results/round3-after-inversion/). Both must stay green.

Round 2/3 evidence layer: the PR's own prototype suite, re-executed by this harness against heads f8d67fa7 and d1c331ae in both gate configurations. Round 3 adds TestAPITransformInformerScope (diw-zw's scope-mismatch ask: the NewInformer hook now wraps only *corev1.Pod ListerWatchers; Service updates flow through the default informer untouched, non-Pod transform calls == 0, with and without the relist probe). These prove the design-level fixes of round-1 findings A-F5, B-F1/B-F2, the admission-rule table incl. ownerReference conditions, and the round-3 informer scoping.

Guard tests: they PASS on base and head by design (they pin the label-selector semantics the KEP builds on). They are not bug repros; treat FIXED here as 'semantics unchanged'. A flip means the vendored client-go changed selector semantics.

liveNote: No live layer: the PR ships a design (keps/284-pod-cache-filter/**) plus a tagged prototype (test/podcacheunion) and changes no runtime code, so there is nothing to exercise against a real cluster. When the implementation PR lands, graft this harness onto it: F1's contract tests and TestCacheOptionsConstrainsPodCache must be green, TestGroupNameDriftStillDetected must stay green, and the read-path audit (R2-F3's corrected claim) must be recorded with its regression test.
